subject: Novum pilot: dedicated capacity sizing & SLO headroom
messages:
From: Ethan Torres <ethan.torres@novum.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot ask: sizing for dedicated GPUs + p95 target (Novum)

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Novum is moving forward with a 3-month pilot and we need a firm recommendation on dedicated capacity sizing so we can finalize the procurement timeline. High-level constraints:
- Expected MAU -> ~120k (weekdays), peak concurrent requests anticipated during product launch window.
- Peak model mix: routing ~60% short-chat, 30% medium summaries, 10% long-context LTR (80k token episodes during batch jobs).
- Target SLOs: p95 response latency <= 250ms for short-chat and <= 650ms for long-context summarization (we can accept longer for batch jobs).
- Desired headroom: something we can present to finance that avoids frequent top-ups — aiming for a 35-50% buffer above expected peak.

Can you map this to tokens/sec, recommended GPUs, and confirm whether the SLOs are realistic without premium burst pricing? Also send any artifacts we can attach to the procurement packet (simple capacity table + expected monthly token burn).

Appreciate it — Ethan
Ethan Torres
Head of Platform
Novum AI

-----Original Message-----

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Torres <ethan.torres@novum.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jan 2027 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot ask: sizing for dedicated GPUs + p95 target (Novum)

Ethan — thanks, clear ask. Quick summary up front: yes, we can meet the short-chat p95 <= 250ms on a Dedicated slab without burst pricing if you accept a conservative slab sized for 40% headroom. Below is our modeling with assumptions called out. I attached a one-page matrix and a short latency-fit PDF for your packet.

Key assumptions (what we used to estimate tokens/sec):
- Short-chat average payload = 55 tokens in + 30 tokens generated = ~85 tokens/req.
- Medium summaries avg payload = 250 tokens in + 180 tokens generated = ~430 tokens/req.
- Long-context batch jobs are scheduled off-peak (average effective throughput window treated separately).
- Model family: mix tested on Llama2-13B-Chat (quantized) and a trimmed Mistral-7B variant; numbers below are blended to represent your stated mix.

High-level tokens/sec mapping (observed in our benchmarks):
- H100 80GB (quantized-opt): ~22,000 tokens/sec sustained per GPU for short-chat-like requests (small context, batch=4).
- A100 80GB (q8): ~12,000 tokens/sec sustained per GPU for mixed loads.
- T4-class (quantized): ~3,000-4,500 tokens/sec (not recommended for headroom-sensitive pilots).

Estimate for Novum peak demand (conservative):
- Peak concurrent QPS (user-facing short-chat spikes): 110 requests/sec -> at 85 tokens/req = 9,350 tokens/sec of generation.
- Medium summaries spike: 30 req/sec -> 12,900 tokens/sec.
- Combined blended peak tokens/sec ~22,250 tokens/sec.

Sizing recommendation (to hit p95 <= 250ms for short-chat):
- Option A (headroom-first): 2 x H100 (80GB) dedicated slab (sustained ~44k tokens/sec) -> gives ~98% runway against blended peak with ~50% headroom.
- Option B (cost-conscious): 4 x A100 (80GB) (sustained ~48k tokens/sec aggregate) with careful batching/kv-cache warming -> roughly comparable headroom but higher operational latency variance on p95 due to longer kv warm.

Why H100 x2 is attractive: fewer nodes reduces KV cache warm cycles, simplifies routing, and keeps p95 tail tight. For your p95 targets we recommend the H100 slab unless you have strict cost ceilings.

Burst policy note: we expose a soft burst lane (pay-as-you-consume) for occasional peaks; but for procurement, a Dedicated slab sized per Option A removes burst uncertainty.

Attachments: novum-sizing-matrix.xlsx (matrix with tokens/sec per GPU and slab cost estimates), latency-fit-20270124.pdf (p95 fit plots).

Next steps:
- If you are comfortable with Option A, we can draft the SOW and start provisioning; provisioning lead time for H100 dedicated nodes is ~2-3 weeks under current supply.
- If you want an alternative with a deeper cost/throughput trade table we can have Karthik run a quick sensitivity simulation tomorrow.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Torres <ethan.torres@novum.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot ask: sizing for dedicated GPUs + p95 target (Novum)

Adding a few concrete knobs and a short sensitivity run I just completed:

Sensitivity run notes (blend model):
- Baseline blended peak tokens/sec used = 22,250 tps (matches Markus numbers).
- Assumed request distribution across slab: short-chat traffic is latency-sensitive and gets sticky routing to warm KV caches.

Observed per-GPU effective throughput at batch targets: (numbers are conservative sustained estimates)
- H100-80GB (Llama2-13B quantized, batch=4): 20k tokens/sec sustained; single-GPU p95 for short-chat ~180-220ms when routing sticky.
- A100-80GB (same model): ~11.5k tokens/sec sustained; p95 ~220-320ms depending on KV cache hit rate.

Slab suggestions with headroom math:
- Conservative target for Novum = blended peak * 1.40 (40% headroom) -> 31,150 tokens/sec requirement.
- Map to H100s: ceil(31,150 / 20,000) = 2 H100 GPUs (gives ~40% headroom). If you want 50% headroom, move to 3 GPUs.
- Map to A100s: ceil(31,150 / 11,500) = 3 A100 GPUs (3xA100 gives ~10% extra headroom beyond 40%).

Operational suggestions:
- Sticky routing for short-chat (pin to a small set of replica slices) preserves low p95; avoid full-fanout routing for these requests.
- Pre-warm KV cache during launch windows using synthetic warmers (we can provide a script included in the sizing matrix).
- Reserve a small soft-burst lane (1 GPU equivalent) for unexpected traffic while you validate traffic shape in week 1. That lane triggers pay-as-you-go billing only when used.

I'll attach a quick sensitivity CSV in the sizing matrix under the "ops" tab. If you want I can run the same sim under a 60% long-context mix to show worst-case.

-Karthik
Principal Capacity Engineer
